summary_en: This study tests abemaciclib, a drug currently used to treat a type of breast cancer, in people with Kaposi sarcoma, with or without HIV. Participants take abemaciclib tablets by mouth every day in 28-day cycles, and treatment continues until the cancer gets worse or side effects are unacceptable. The study aims to find a safe dose and see whether abemaciclib can shrink lesions or tumors; it is a Phase 1/2 study.
summary_es: Este estudio prueba abemaciclib, un medicamento que actualmente se usa para tratar un tipo de cáncer de mama, en personas con sarcoma de Kaposi, con o sin VIH. Los participantes toman tabletas de abemaciclib por vía oral todos los días, en ciclos de 28 días, y el tratamiento continúa hasta que el cáncer empeore o los efectos secundarios sean inaceptables. El estudio busca encontrar una dosis segura y ver si abemaciclib puede reducir las lesiones o los tumores; es un estudio de Fase 1/2.
who_for: Kaposi sarcoma confirmed by the NCI pathology laboratory.
At least five measurable skin lesions, or evaluable disease per RECIST criteria.
Age 18 or older; HIV-positive or HIV-negative participants may enroll.
Adequate blood counts, liver, kidney and heart function as defined in the record.
Able to swallow oral medicine; ECOG performance status 2 or better.
not_for: Chemotherapy or immunotherapy within 3 weeks before study entry.
Radiotherapy without completing recovery and a washout of at least 14 days.
Pregnancy, or nursing while treated with abemaciclib.
Severe allergy to similar CDK inhibitor compounds, or interstitial lung disease.
